text:
{
  "background_info": "Student Name: Arjun Sharma
Grade / Age: Grade 4 / 10 years
School: Delhi Public School, Bengaluru
Date of IEP Meeting: 19 October 2026
Disability Classification: Specific Learning Disability (Dyslexia, Moderate) under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
Dominant Language: English
Date Services Begin: 2 November 2026
Parent/Guardian Contact: Mr. and Mrs. Sharma (contact details maintained on school register)
Medical Alerts: No medical alerts or known allergies; student experiences heightened academic anxiety during unassisted reading and writing tasks.",

  "academic_performance": "Present Level: Academic/Educational Achievement - Arjun Sharma is currently functioning below grade level in reading decoding, reading fluency, and written expression, while functioning at or above grade level in mathematics, demonstrating strong numerical calculations and spatial reasoning. In English, Arjun exhibits significant decoding barriers and frequent visual-motor letter reversals involving 'b/d' and 'p/q' in written assignments.
Present Level: Cognitive Ability - Arjun Sharma is currently functioning at grade level in intellectual and cognitive capabilities, displaying superior verbal comprehension, exceptional auditory memory, and sharp analytical thinking during structured oral discussions.
Present Level: Language Ability - Arjun Sharma is currently functioning at grade level in receptive and expressive oral language, expressing complex ideas articulately, but functions below grade level in written orthography and phonological decoding.
Present Level: Learning Style - Arjun Sharma is an auditory and kinesthetic learner who processes and retains complex information best through verbal discussions, listening, and hands-on spatial tasks rather than text-heavy reading.
Present Level: Rate of Progress - Arjun Sharma is currently demonstrating a stable rate of progress in oral and conceptual areas, but demonstrates slow progress in independent reading and writing tasks due to decoding fatigue and task-avoidance behaviors.",

  "social_development": "Present Level: Relationships with Peers and Adults - Arjun Sharma establishes positive, cooperative relationships with classmates and school staff. He participates enthusiastically in cooperative group activities and classroom discussions, demonstrating leadership and collaborative teamwork.
Present Level: Self-Concept - Arjun demonstrates healthy self-esteem during oral discussions and mathematical problem solving, but exhibits marked self-doubt, vulnerability, and academic anxiety when requested to read aloud or complete written tasks independently.
Present Level: Behaviors That Impede Learning - Arjun loses focus and exhibits avoidance behaviors, such as restlessness and task delays, specifically during independent reading and text-dense writing activities, reflecting frustration with printed materials rather than disruptive behavioral intent.",

  "physical_development": "Present Level: Motor and Sensory Development - Arjun demonstrates age-appropriate gross motor skills, physical stamina, and sensory awareness, participating actively in physical education and outdoor activities. In fine motor and visual-motor integration, Arjun demonstrates persistent letter reversals ('b/d' and 'p/q') and visual-motor coordination strain during pencil-and-paper writing, reflecting the visual-orthographic processing challenges characteristic of his moderate dyslexia diagnosis. He benefits from occupational therapy consultation and tactile-kinesthetic writing scaffolds to support visual-spatial coordination.",

  "management_needs": "Arjun requires a moderate level of environmental modifications and human/material resources to participate successfully in the curriculum. His environmental needs include preferential seating in the front row near the instructor to minimize visual distractions, an organized workspace, and visual graphic organizers to structure academic expectations.
Material and human resource needs encompass specialised instruction by a trained special educator, multi-sensory structured literacy materials, assistive technology software, and consultative support from an occupational therapist and school counsellor to address directional letter reversals and performance anxiety.",

  "long_term_outcomes": "N/A — Student is below 14 years. Long-term adult outcomes and transition planning will be developed at age 14 per RPwD Act 2016 and NCTE Guidelines.",

  "annual_goals": "Annual Goal: Arjun will apply multi-sensory decoding strategies to independently read grade-level narrative and informational passages at 80 words correct per minute with 90% accuracy as measured by quarterly curriculum-based reading fluency probes.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Arjun will independently decode 40 phonetically regular multi-syllabic words with 80% accuracy across 4 consecutive weekly trials as measured by special educator running records.
2. By the end of Term 2, Arjun will read grade-level passage segments using a text-to-speech support tool and answer 80% of comprehension questions correctly in 3 consecutive assessments as measured by teacher-recorded rubrics.
3. By the end of Term 3, Arjun will independently decode unfamiliar grade-level words in connected text at 80 words correct per minute with 90% accuracy in 4 out of 5 trials as measured by curriculum-based fluency probes.
Evaluation Procedures: Running records, curriculum-based fluency probes, teacher-recorded rubrics
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: Arjun will compose structured multi-sentence paragraphs using visual graphic organizers and assistive writing tools with correct letter orientation and fewer than 2 reversals per page with 85% accuracy as measured by writing portfolio rubrics.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Arjun will correctly differentiate and write letters b, d, p, and q with 85% accuracy in 4 out of 5 trials as measured by weekly spelling and writing work samples.
2. By the end of Term 2, Arjun will plan and draft a 5-sentence structured paragraph using a visual graphic organizer and speech-to-text software with 80% syntactical accuracy in 3 consecutive work samples as measured by writing rubric analysis.
3. By the end of Term 3, Arjun will independently compose a structured multi-paragraph written response using assistive speech-to-text or graphic organizers, achieving a passing grade of 70% or higher as measured by term-end academic evaluations.
Evaluation Procedures: Work sample analysis, rubric scoring, writing portfolio assessment
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: Arjun will utilize self-advocacy and coping strategies to initiate reading and writing tasks within 3 minutes and sustain active attention for 20 minutes across 80% of observed classroom periods as measured by monthly teacher behavior logs.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Arjun will identify feelings of academic frustration and independently request a designated break or tactile tool within 2 minutes of task presentation in 4 out of 5 observed instances as measured by teacher observation checklists.
2. By the end of Term 2, Arjun will independently access text-to-speech software or a graphic organizer within 3 minutes of assignment distribution without avoidance behaviors in 80% of opportunities as measured by classroom tracking sheets.
3. By the end of Term 3, Arjun will maintain sustained on-task engagement during independent reading or writing tasks for at least 20 consecutive minutes with no more than 1 redirection in 4 out of 5 trials as measured by structured interval recording logs.
Evaluation Procedures: Behavioral observation logs, self-monitoring checklists, interval recording data
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly",

  "special_education_services": "A. Special education programs with frequency and duration, beginning 2 November 2026 and continuing through 31 March 2027:
Specialised instruction by trained special educator utilizing a multi-sensory structured literacy approach (Orton-Gillingham methodology) for 45 minutes per session, 4 sessions per week in the resource room, beginning 2 November 2026 and continuing through 31 March 2027. Access to specialized therapeutic services (occupational and speech support) in accordance with NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30), comprising weekly 45-minute occupational therapy sessions to remediate visual-motor letter reversals and consultative speech-language support. Counselling or social-emotional support provided by the school counsellor for 30 minutes once weekly to address task-related anxiety. In accordance with NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 32), the team will monitor the nature, frequency, and extent of required support on a bi-weekly basis and strengthen interventions as needed.

B. Extended school year services: No. Arjun does not exhibit severe regression over breaks that would necessitate extended school year services.

C. Supplementary aids and modifications:
Provision of multi-sensory structured literacy and assistive text-to-speech/speech-to-text tools with RPwD Act Section 31 appropriate environment mandate; visual templates and graphic organizers for writing assignments; preferential seating near the front of the room; oral alternatives for demonstrating subject mastery; reduced pencil-and-paper homework volume; and audio versions of textbooks.

D. Assistive technology devices/services:
Assistive technology as appropriate to disability, including digital tablets and computers equipped with text-to-speech and speech-to-text software tools, speech-recognition dictation tools, electronic graphic organization templates, and audiobooks with highlighted text tracking.

E. Program modifications for school personnel:
Bi-monthly consultation between the special educator, occupational therapist, and general education teachers on dyslexia-friendly pedagogical adaptations, multi-sensory teaching strategies, and grading adjustments.

F. Individual testing modifications:
Extended time (minimum 25%) on all assessments; separate, quiet testing environment with reduced sensory stimuli; oral reading of test instructions and questions; permission to utilize assistive speech-to-text tools or an approved scribe; and inclusive and flexible assessment tools providing continuous feedback per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30).",

  "general_education_participation": "Arjun will participate in general education classes for approximately 80% of the instructional week, including Mathematics, Science/Environmental Studies, Social Sciences, Physical Education, Visual Arts, and co-curricular programs. He will receive pull-out specialised instruction in the resource room for 20% of the week (four 45-minute sessions weekly) for intensive multi-sensory literacy intervention.

No second-language exemption is granted at this stage; Arjun will participate in the standard language curriculum alongside peers, supported by differentiated instructional materials, multi-sensory strategies, speech-to-text technology, and adjusted grading rubrics.",

  "participating_agencies": "N/A — Transition services not yet applicable. Will be identified at age 14.",

  "coordinated_activities": "1. Instruction: Specialised multi-sensory literacy instruction provided in the resource room by the special educator and differentiated instruction within the general classroom.
2. Related Services: Occupational therapy services for visual-motor letter reversals, speech support consultation per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30), and weekly school counselling for anxiety reduction.
3. Employment/Post-secondary Education: N/A — Student is 10 years of age.
4. Community Experience: N/A — Student is 10 years of age.
5. Activities of Daily Living: Explicit instruction in classroom organization, notebook management, and digital device usage routines.
6. Functional Vocational Assessment: N/A — Student is 10 years of age.",

  "graduation_info": "Certificate sought: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) Secondary School Certificate.
Expected year of school completion: March 2033.
Board examination provisions under RPwD Act accommodations: Standard CBSE board examination accommodations for candidates with Specific Learning Disabilities (Dyslexia), including extended compensatory time (minimum 25%), separate quiet examination hall, permission to utilize a computer with assistive text-to-speech and speech-to-text software or a scribe, and inclusive assessment formatting. In alignment with Section 6, no second-language exemption is granted; Arjun will complete standard curriculum requirements with approved testing accommodations.",

  "recommendations_summary": "Disability classification: Specific Learning Disability (Dyslexia, Moderate) under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 Schedule.
Recommended placement: Inclusive general education setting with resource room support (80% general education, 20% special education resource setting), fulfilling the mandate for free education in an appropriate environment under RPwD Act Section 31.
Curriculum exemptions: No second-language exemption is granted; standard curriculum with multi-sensory and assistive accommodations.
Extended school year services: Not required.
Transportation needs: Standard school transport without specialized modifications.
Annual IEP review: 19 October 2027.",

  "progress_reporting": "Arjun's progress toward his annual goals and short-term objectives will be reported to his parents with the same frequency as non-disabled peers, through term-end academic report cards issued at the end of each academic term.

In addition to standard report cards, parents will receive comprehensive written progress reports detailing Arjun's mastery of each short-term objective using inclusive and flexible assessment tools providing continuous feedback per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30).

Criteria for measuring progress will consist of objective curriculum-based measurement probes, running records, writing portfolio evaluations, and behavioral observation data. Formal parent-teacher-specialist conferences will be convened at the end of each term, with interim updates shared bi-weekly through the home-school communication log."
}
